1	# Front-end and design-ideation evaluation of the Wisp plugins
2	
3	Status: evidence base and plan, with Wave 0 and the core of Wave 1 built (see `IMPLEMENTATION-LOG.md`). Done: the Codex role-card model ids, generated Claude manifests with validation, platform-limit and cross-reference checks, a reasoning-wording lint, the `muse` gate aligned to `verdict@3`, tools for transcript metrics and paired analysis, registers of assumptions and verified facts, and the exploration modes (`muse/sketch`, `muse/promote`, `smith/spike`, the `explorer` agent, two new schemas, ADR 011), each piloted once. Nothing is released: no plugin version, changelog or tag changed. The rest of the 172 work packages below are awaiting a decision or not started. ADR 011 was written as Accepted by the author and needs review.
4	
5	## Why this exists
6	
7	The plugins were used on two brand sites (techworx and orin-dx). This evaluation reads the sessions and repos from that work, surveys how the industry does agentic design and front-end work, and turns both into a sequenced plan. The trigger was a user observation: the plugin workflows are too rigid for early, experimental, idea-flushing work, where the goal is to see designs and check that tools work without specs, tests or gates.
8	
9	## Contents
10	
11	| Path | What it is |
12	| :-- | :-- |
13	| `CATALOG.md` | The plan: 144 work packages, a dependency graph, six waves, 10 proposed ADRs, 20 conflicts with resolutions, and post-verification amendments (section 5) |
14	| `IMPLEMENTATION-LOG.md` | What Wave 0 changed so far, what it found, the change record the repo requires, and the release bookkeeping deliberately not done |
15	| `ARCHITECTURE-REVIEW.md` | Each architectural assumption tested against what current agent platforms can do, measured repo facts, 28 more work packages (WP-601 to WP-628, 172 in total) added by the review and its verification, and the resulting direction: thinner prompts, thicker harness. Its section 7.1 overrides earlier rows where verification corrected them |
16	| `traceability/` | Five matrices mapping about 1,000 individual findings to WPs, each with contradictions, claims to verify, and proposed new WPs. `WP-draft.md` is the first draft the matrices were built against |
17	| `verification/` | `VERIFY-1.md` (transcript and repo claims), `VERIFY-2.md` (web and documentation claims), `VERIFY-3.md` (first-hand measurements: refusal scan, live probe, gate cost, repo structure), `Y1` to `Y6` (full primary-source reads of Claude Code, Anthropic, Codex, AGY and standards, design sources, aviation and evals), and `scripts/` that reproduce the measurements. They correct errors in the evidence notes |
18	| `evidence/` | The raw research notes. Index and tag legend in `evidence/README.md` |
19	
20	Paths written `<refs>/...` in the catalog and matrices are *proposed* reference files that do not exist yet. The repo's reference-integrity test validates every literal `shared/references/` path, so proposals are marked this way.
21	
22	Read in this order: this file, then `CATALOG.md` sections 3 to 5, then `verification/`, then a matrix when you need the source of a specific WP.
23	
24	## What the sessions show
25	
26	Scope: about 812 transcript files, but only a handful are real top-level sessions; the rest are subagent transcripts. Plugin agents were used in two sessions: `orin-dx` b8d16e96 (09-29 to 10-03) and `pages` 24655582 (10-05 to 10-16). `vanguard` ran once, on 10-17, for blog-topic research. Everything else, including nearly all design ideation, used no plugin.
27	
28	1. **Strong on behavior, blind on appearance.** Gates caught real contradictions, accessibility values (a 2.82:1 contrast failure recomputed from the token source), and cross-spec conflicts. Every visible defect was found by a human look, an audit, or the 16 Oct suite. `spec@1` has no way to express visual intent and nothing renders anything.
29	2. **Gate loops were fix-and-resubmit.** 38 gate calls in the `orin-dx` session (28 muse, 10 scribe) and 51 `muse:exit-gate` calls in the `pages` session (per spec: 7, 5, 6, 9, 4, 6, 8, 6 for SPEC-005 to 012, inside a 57-minute window). Every spec failed its first gate with 9 to 23 blockers. The retry cap of 3 was not enforced: gates said "escalate" from retry 4 and the orchestrator continued with no user message in between (SPEC-005 ended at retry 6, SPEC-008 at 9). All eight specs finished as passes with empty blockers.
30	3. **Approval in prose failed.** The user repeatedly asked to see rendered examples (the session matrix counts at least seven requests; not independently re-counted) and the agent described first. Drawn prototypes then exposed a touch-target bug the gated spec missed.
31	4. **Specs lagged the design.** Specs gated on 11 Oct were rewritten the next day after decisions made from drawn pages, and the 12 Oct revisions ran with "no exit gate this round". SPEC-013 supersedes much of SPEC-001 and SPEC-003c.
32	5. **Exploration worked best outside the plugins.** Option boards (Artifacts in Oct, repo-script Playwright screenshots, local pages) and short answer codes. The user stated the two-phase model explicitly on 2026-10-14 at 20:25 UTC (`pages` line 49946): exploratory build quick, specs and tests when it narrows. The same session built the landing, Tools and Principles pages in about 30 minutes once the audit machinery stopped.
33	6. **Ceremony still paid off for stable contracts.** The SiteNav migration passed 478 Chromium e2e tests, and the challenger found real plan defects.
34	7. **Defects shipped past the gates** (documented in commits whose hashes were confirmed to exist): "NaN%" glass opacity on the Orin brand page, card strand fades that cut hard at phone width, tool marks stretched and 2px low, colour-card labels at 2.9 to 4.3:1 contrast, a filter 1px short of the 44px target, duplicate banner landmarks, and misattributed decisions in case-study copy.
35	8. **Stalls and unused agents.** The `orin-dx` session had 17 failed agent tasks (11 watchdog stalls, 6 API errors); the `pages` session had none. `smith:recon` and every `sentinel:*` agent appear in no transcript, `smith:reviewer`, `smith:mutator` and `smith:exit-gate` ran only in a third project, and the cause is unknown (WP-56).
36	
37	## What the plugins lack, by design
38	
39	- No browser, screenshot, Storybook or visual capability anywhere; the `workspace-manifest@1` capability list is closed and cannot record one.
40	- No schema for a direction, brief, wireframe, prototype, copy deck or critique, and no divergent cognitive mode.
41	- Muse's docs point three times to "ranger's accessibility hazard taxonomy"; ranger has none, so implemented accessibility is never checked (WP-01, WP-44).
42	- Every build path runs recon, mutation, review and a binding exit-gate; there is no spike or sketch mode. Constitution rules (default-fail gates, no TBDs) make an unfinished idea an invalid artifact.
43	- 29 of 31 schemas carry a mandatory `reasoning` scratchpad field (constitution line 242). Anthropic's refusals documentation names a `reasoning`, `thinking` or `trace` field as a `reasoning_extraction` trigger. First-hand evidence (`verification/VERIFY-3.md`): zero refusals in 72k+ Sonnet 5.5 and Opus 5.5 messages from the sessions, and a live probe in which the real `muse:drafter` prompt with its scratchpad field completed normally twice while one added line demanding verbatim chain of thought was refused and billed. The trigger is wording that asks for reproduced reasoning, not the field's existence. WP-625 adds a wording lint and a per-model-generation probe.
44	
45	## What the industry shows
46	
47	Corrected after verification; see `verification/VERIFY-2.md` for evidence.
48	
49	- **Intent and behavior are separate artifacts** (DESIGN.md, uSpec, Storybook, Atlassian). `spec@1` mixes them and can express only behavior.
50	- **Extract deterministically, then let the model add judgment** (uSpec; Netflix and JetBrains code intelligence; Spectrum's generated skills). It maps to the stale-number problem in the specs.
51	- **Render, then compare** is the standard verification loop, and Anthropic's own guidance recommends giving the agent a way to verify its work. A clean axe run covers about 57% of accessibility issues by volume (Deque, 2021).
52	- **Lint is the preferred gate** (Salesforce, Primer, Spectrum, Vercel). Gates that only judge text miss rendered defects.
53	- **Mode routing separates exploring from hardening** (Vercel's product-design skill: shape, implement, review, copy, harden; exploration modes make no edits).
54	- **A monolithic DESIGN.md is costly:** Atlassian measured 7.21M tokens against 3.75M for MCP, 4.43M for a skill and 4.20M for no context on one task. Vercel's design.md showed 39 vs 91 failures but on six pages, so it is weak evidence either way. Use a small routed intent file and lookups, and run our own paired test (WP-402).
55	- **Nobody has a real decision log.** Claude Design has no version history and Figma Make users ask for branching.
56	- **Token-saving prompts and tools do little in agentic work.** Caveman: about 8.5% output tokens on 82 paired tasks with no detectable quality change (JetBrains, Sonnet 5 at low effort, a ceiling because activation was forced). rtk: no token saving and a +7.6% cost at low effort (p=0.004), none at high effort; its own `rtk gain` scoreboard reported 96.2M tokens saved while the bill rose. The method is the reusable part: paired runs, medians, bill-based, failures excluded from both arms, and never trusting k=1.
57	- **Corrections from verification:** 15 of 21 design systems ship `llms.txt` (not "almost none"); Coinbase's Code Connect figures are +1 quality point, -29.5% tokens and -19.6% duration over 27 tasks on two design systems; v0 Design Systems 2.0 launched 2026-06-25; the Figma Starter limit is 20 calls per month; `test-run` is the Storybook MCP tool name; WCAG 2.5.8 is AA at 24x24 and the 44x44 figure is 2.5.5 at AAA; Codex custom agents are natively TOML (repo policy still keeps role cards markdown).
58	- **Not found:** first-party Airbnb or Netflix design-system AI material (Netflix's JetBrains case study concerns Java code intelligence), and verified Shopify design-rules material. These are dispositions in the matrices, not silent omissions.
59	
60	## The plan
61	
62	144 work packages from the evidence mapping, none dropped, plus 28 from the architecture review and its verification (172 in total). Eight overlap another WP and are merged into it with a reason; about 20 more overlap and are kept with the reason stated. Full table in `CATALOG.md`.
63	
64	| Wave | Theme | WPs | Needs first |
65	| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
66	| 0 | Defects, baselines, measurement | 21 | nothing |
67	| 1 | Exploration modes (the stated priority) | 19 | ADR N1 |
68	| 2 | Gate hygiene and orchestration | 27 | ADR N4, N5 |
69	| 3 | Visual intent and evidence | 43 | ADR N2, N3 (one schema bundle) |
70	| 4 | Prompt, model, Codex, AGENTS.md, distribution | 27 | ADR N8, N9, N10 (conditional) |
71	| 5 | Consumer-repo and research follow-ups | 7 | nothing |
72	
73	Highlights:
74	- **Wave 0:** fix the muse dangling reference and move muse to `verdict@3`; baseline the gate metrics from transcripts; build the paired-eval harness; test the `reasoning` refusal risk first (WP-61); find why agents went unused (WP-56).
75	- **Wave 1:** a mode router (shape, sketch, spike, implement, review, copy, harden, promote); a `sketch` skill with durable option files (stable ids, status, one-line reason) that double as the decision log, rendered locally as a brand x theme x viewport matrix, TBDs allowed, no gate; a smith `spike` skill to check that a tool or library works; a show-first rule; direction-commit and anti-slop controls; a lightweight promote (WP-14a) that carries a chosen option forward as a requirement plus a brief.
76	- **Wave 2:** evidence-citing blockers, "no findings" as a valid pass, enforced retry caps with logged overrides, readback in correction loops, a small fixed vocabulary, stall procedures, orchestrator-owned spawning, and file ownership for parallel work.
77	- **Wave 3:** `spec@2` with token and visual references, a render-evidence artifact and manifest capability, deterministic UI checks (tokens, contrast, target size, landmarks, copy provenance), the full promote path, a visual critic, and ground-truth extraction before drafting.
78	- **Wave 4:** ablations of the constitution and prompt structure measured net of cache hits, tier re-checks per model, Codex role cards, an AGENTS.md strategy, and skill versioning and maintenance.
79	
80	Design choices made in the catalog's conflict table (section 4): 3 options per round and 4 directions only at the first direction-commit; 3 parallel writers by default and up to 5 for disjoint work; scanners report everything and a separate stage filters while gates stay scoped to stated requirements (test first in WP-60); no tier changes on vendor claims until measured (WP-63).
81	
82	## Architecture review (summary)
83	
84	Full text in `ARCHITECTURE-REVIEW.md`. Measured facts: 10 plugins, 30 skills, 44 agents; agents use only five frontmatter keys and none of the platform's native controls (`tools`, `maxTurns`, `isolation`, `skills`, `memory`); no plugin ships hooks, validators, workflows or code-intelligence servers.
85	
86	- **Keep:** the schemas as the cross-harness contract, progressive disclosure, and the differentiators no harness provides natively: falsifiable specs, adversarial refutation, fail-by-default binding gates, enforced self-audit.
87	- **Change:** enforcement. Retry caps, schema validity and "no pass without evidence" move from prompts into hooks or workflow scripts where the harness supports it, with the prompt path as the cross-harness fallback (the retry cap failed in the `pages` session because it lived only in a prompt). Plans become outcome-level and resumable for longer autonomous runs. Visual evidence comes from capability-detected native browsers.
88	- **Test before deciding:** whether role-based agent splits pay for their cost (Anthropic recommends splitting by context, not role; multi-agent runs cost 3 to 15 times a single agent). WP-601 sets up `claude plugin eval` with a no-plugin baseline.
89	- **Lower priority than first thought:** the constitution is a 6-line block in each agent, not 290 lines. The 290-line file is the authoring-time rulebook (catalog amendment P8).
90	- **Shape:** Codex has its own native plugin format in `harnesses/codex/`; AGY's format is similar to Claude Code's and shares the authored tree. AGY workflows stop working on 2026-10-19, so author skills only.
91	
92	## Conformance findings from primary-source verification
93	
94	Details in `verification/Y1` to `Y6` and `ARCHITECTURE-REVIEW.md` section 7.1.
95	
96	- **Claude Code.** `claude plugin validate plugins/<id>` reports a pass after checking components only, because the manifests sit at the plugin root and not at `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`. Validated explicitly, each manifest gets 3 warnings (`id`, `consumes`, `produces` are ignored at load time) and `--strict` would fail all 10. Agent `role` and skill `version` frontmatter have no runtime effect. Each plugin's `shared` symlink points outside the plugin directory. Subagents deliver reports through a `SubagentHandback` tool in auto mode (since 2.1.271), so a `SubagentStop` validator would read the wrong field. Stop-hook continuations are hard-capped at 8, and a failing or timed-out hook does not block unless `onFailure: "block"` (needs 2.1.295; local CLI is 2.1.292). The 15,000-token agent-description limit is a startup warning, not an error.
97	- **Codex.** The roles README names retired or unknown model ids (`gpt-5.6-luna`, `-terra`, `-sol`; current: `gpt-6-luna`, `gpt-6.1-sol`, `gpt-6-astra`). 18 skills phrase delegation as "teams" or "teammates"; Codex delegates only when told to, so only the sequential fallback runs today. Role cards cannot enforce read-only (subagents inherit the parent sandbox). Only the legacy `.codex-plugin/plugin.json` exists, and `capabilities` carries an undocumented value (`agent-teams-optional`).
98	- **Antigravity and standards.** The `$schema` URLs in the root `marketplace.json` and AGY's documented plugin schema both return 404, and no third-party AGY marketplace schema is documented, so that file is repo-private. Agent Plugins 1.0.0 requires `$schema` and `name` in its manifest and rejects paths leaving the plugin root. AGY workflows stop on 2026-10-19 (primary page).
99	- **Claims corrected.** The harness-simplification result (6h/$200 vs 3h50m/$124.70) compares different models and prompts and kept the planner and evaluator; the "31-minute UK AISI horizon" is not in the cited paper; "Astra about 40 minutes per task" is a vendor latency simulation, not an autonomy duration; Caveman's "65%" is stale (its repo now reports 3% over a concise-control for the basic mode); `taste-skill` v2 has no dials; "verify" is FAA usage, ICAO and UK material uses "confirm"; AFIS and IFR claims needed qualification.
100	
101	## How the user's guidance is covered
102	
103	| Guidance | Where |
104	| :-- | :-- |
105	| Flexible, "vibe-coded" exploration without worrying about specs and tests | Wave 1: WP-10, 11, 12, 13, 15, 16, 18, 19; mode router gives each mode its own gate set (conflict K12) |
106	| See designs | WP-12 (rendered option matrix, local first), WP-211 (show-first rule), WP-34 |
107	| Validate that tools work | WP-15 smith `spike`: smoke-check evidence, verified-vs-unverified report, promote or discard |
108	| Specs and tests once ideas narrow, without regressions | WP-14a/b promote, WP-19 harden, WP-106 to 108 spec hygiene, WP-204 test taxonomy |
109	| Do not cut things | 144 WPs, 8 merged with reasons, dispositions for items with no action; nothing was dropped |
110	| Learn from industry, model vendors, AGENTS.md, uSpec, ICAO, TanStack Intent | Waves 3 and 4; WP-32 and 33 (uSpec), WP-71 (AGENTS.md), WP-53, 54 and 212 (ICAO ideas), WP-72 (Intent) |
111	
112	## Open items and limits
113	
114	- **Unverified here:** pages commit counts (repo history access was blocked for that repo), the `a859e2f` origin claim, the 271 KB JS budget, whether SPEC-013 supersedes 26 of SPEC-001's and 35 of SPEC-003c's criteria, Shopify and Airbnb figures, the Figma 25k response cap, whether Codex loads Claude agents or hooks from `.claude-plugin` formats, install behavior of the `shared` symlink in each harness, whether `skills-ref` rejects a top-level `version`, and the refusal probe on Opus 5.5 and Fable 5.1 (only Sonnet 5.5 was probed). The aviation items were checked against UK CAP 413 and SKYbrary, not ICAO documents directly; see `verification/Y6-aviation-evals.md`.
115	- **Weak evidence by nature:** vendor self-benchmarks and small samples (Vercel's six pages, Atlassian's single task). WP-401 proposes tagging them.
116	- **One project:** all transcript evidence is from two sessions in one body of work. Gate cost was measured from those sessions (`verification/VERIFY-3.md`) and covers subagent-reported tokens only, not a bill or main-session tokens.
117	- **Not read:** several newer Anthropic posts (infrastructure noise, eval awareness, auto mode), the Codex computer-use and MCP pages and release notes before 0.162, and ICAO Annex 10/11, Doc 4444 and Doc 9432 directly.
118	- **User configuration untouched:** `~/.claude/RTK.md` installs rtk with the same hook JetBrains tested. Whether it helps this workflow is an open paired test (WP-68), not a recommendation to change it.
119	
120	## Next decisions
121	
122	1. Accept or amend the wave order, in particular Wave 1 before Wave 2.
123	2. Write ADR N1 (exploratory mode, amending ADR 003) and N6 (the `reasoning` field policy: keep the field, lint the wording), and start with the Wave 0 conformance fixes (WP-617, WP-620, WP-622, WP-624, WP-625).
124	3. Decide whether sketch and promote live as skills in `muse` (which already owns UI) or in a new plugin; `AGENTS.md` allows several skills in one plugin when intents are heterogeneous, and the catalog assumes `muse`.
125

## What the sessions show

Scope: about 812 transcript files, but only a handful are real top-level sessions; the rest are subagent transcripts. Plugin agents were used in two sessions: `orin-dx` b8d16e96 (09-29 to 10-03) and `pages` 24655582 (10-05 to 10-16). `vanguard` ran once, on 10-17, for blog-topic research. Everything else, including nearly all design ideation, used no plugin.

1. **Strong on behavior, blind on appearance.** Gates caught real contradictions, accessibility values (a 2.82:1 contrast failure recomputed from the token source), and cross-spec conflicts. Every visible defect was found by a human look, an audit, or the 16 Oct suite. `spec@1` has no way to express visual intent and nothing renders anything.
2. **Gate loops were fix-and-resubmit.** 38 gate calls in the `orin-dx` session (28 muse, 10 scribe) and 51 `muse:exit-gate` calls in the `pages` session (per spec: 7, 5, 6, 9, 4, 6, 8, 6 for SPEC-005 to 012, inside a 57-minute window). Every spec failed its first gate with 9 to 23 blockers. The retry cap of 3 was not enforced: gates said "escalate" from retry 4 and the orchestrator continued with no user message in between (SPEC-005 ended at retry 6, SPEC-008 at 9). All eight specs finished as passes with empty blockers.
3. **Approval in prose failed.** The user repeatedly asked to see rendered examples (the session matrix counts at least seven requests; not independently re-counted) and the agent described first. Drawn prototypes then exposed a touch-target bug the gated spec missed.
4. **Specs lagged the design.** Specs gated on 11 Oct were rewritten the next day after decisions made from drawn pages, and the 12 Oct revisions ran with "no exit gate this round". SPEC-013 supersedes much of SPEC-001 and SPEC-003c.
5. **Exploration worked best outside the plugins.** Option boards (Artifacts in Oct, repo-script Playwright screenshots, local pages) and short answer codes. The user stated the two-phase model explicitly on 2026-10-14 at 20:25 UTC (`pages` line 49946): exploratory build quick, specs and tests when it narrows. The same session built the landing, Tools and Principles pages in about 30 minutes once the audit machinery stopped.
6. **Ceremony still paid off for stable contracts.** The SiteNav migration passed 478 Chromium e2e tests, and the challenger found real plan defects.
7. **Defects shipped past the gates** (documented in commits whose hashes were confirmed to exist): "NaN%" glass opacity on the Orin brand page, card strand fades that cut hard at phone width, tool marks stretched and 2px low, colour-card labels at 2.9 to 4.3:1 contrast, a filter 1px short of the 44px target, duplicate banner landmarks, and misattributed decisions in case-study copy.
8. **Stalls and unused agents.** The `orin-dx` session had 17 failed agent tasks (11 watchdog stalls, 6 API errors); the `pages` session had none. `smith:recon` and every `sentinel:*` agent appear in no transcript, `smith:reviewer`, `smith:mutator` and `smith:exit-gate` ran only in a third project, and the cause is unknown (WP-56).

## What the plugins lack, by design

- No browser, screenshot, Storybook or visual capability anywhere; the `workspace-manifest@1` capability list is closed and cannot record one.
- No schema for a direction, brief, wireframe, prototype, copy deck or critique, and no divergent cognitive mode.
- Muse's docs point three times to "ranger's accessibility hazard taxonomy"; ranger has none, so implemented accessibility is never checked (WP-01, WP-44).
- Every build path runs recon, mutation, review and a binding exit-gate; there is no spike or sketch mode. Constitution rules (default-fail gates, no TBDs) make an unfinished idea an invalid artifact.
- 29 of 31 schemas carry a mandatory `reasoning` scratchpad field (constitution line 242). Anthropic's refusals documentation names a `reasoning`, `thinking` or `trace` field as a `reasoning_extraction` trigger. First-hand evidence (`verification/VERIFY-3.md`): zero refusals in 72k+ Sonnet 5.5 and Opus 5.5 messages from the sessions, and a live probe in which the real `muse:drafter` prompt with its scratchpad field completed normally twice while one added line demanding verbatim chain of thought was refused and billed. The trigger is wording that asks for reproduced reasoning, not the field's existence. WP-625 adds a wording lint and a per-model-generation probe.

## What the industry shows

Corrected after verification; see `verification/VERIFY-2.md` for evidence.

- **Intent and behavior are separate artifacts** (DESIGN.md, uSpec, Storybook, Atlassian). `spec@1` mixes them and can express only behavior.
- **Extract deterministically, then let the model add judgment** (uSpec; Netflix and JetBrains code intelligence; Spectrum's generated skills). It maps to the stale-number problem in the specs.
- **Render, then compare** is the standard verification loop, and Anthropic's own guidance recommends giving the agent a way to verify its work. A clean axe run covers about 57% of accessibility issues by volume (Deque, 2021).
- **Lint is the preferred gate** (Salesforce, Primer, Spectrum, Vercel). Gates that only judge text miss rendered defects.
- **Mode routing separates exploring from hardening** (Vercel's product-design skill: shape, implement, review, copy, harden; exploration modes make no edits).
- **A monolithic DESIGN.md is costly:** Atlassian measured 7.21M tokens against 3.75M for MCP, 4.43M for a skill and 4.20M for no context on one task. Vercel's design.md showed 39 vs 91 failures but on six pages, so it is weak evidence either way. Use a small routed intent file and lookups, and run our own paired test (WP-402).
- **Nobody has a real decision log.** Claude Design has no version history and Figma Make users ask for branching.
- **Token-saving prompts and tools do little in agentic work.** Caveman: about 8.5% output tokens on 82 paired tasks with no detectable quality change (JetBrains, Sonnet 5 at low effort, a ceiling because activation was forced). rtk: no token saving and a +7.6% cost at low effort (p=0.004), none at high effort; its own `rtk gain` scoreboard reported 96.2M tokens saved while the bill rose. The method is the reusable part: paired runs, medians, bill-based, failures excluded from both arms, and never trusting k=1.
- **Corrections from verification:** 15 of 21 design systems ship `llms.txt` (not "almost none"); Coinbase's Code Connect figures are +1 quality point, -29.5% tokens and -19.6% duration over 27 tasks on two design systems; v0 Design Systems 2.0 launched 2026-06-25; the Figma Starter limit is 20 calls per month; `test-run` is the Storybook MCP tool name; WCAG 2.5.8 is AA at 24x24 and the 44x44 figure is 2.5.5 at AAA; Codex custom agents are natively TOML (repo policy still keeps role cards markdown).
- **Not found:** first-party Airbnb or Netflix design-system AI material (Netflix's JetBrains case study concerns Java code intelligence), and verified Shopify design-rules material. These are dispositions in the matrices, not silent omissions.

## The plan

144 work packages from the evidence mapping, none dropped, plus 28 from the architecture review and its verification (172 in total). Eight overlap another WP and are merged into it with a reason; about 20 more overlap and are kept with the reason stated. Full table in `CATALOG.md`.

| Wave | Theme | WPs | Needs first |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| 0 | Defects, baselines, measurement | 21 | nothing |
| 1 | Exploration modes (the stated priority) | 19 | ADR N1 |
| 2 | Gate hygiene and orchestration | 27 | ADR N4, N5 |
| 3 | Visual intent and evidence | 43 | ADR N2, N3 (one schema bundle) |
| 4 | Prompt, model, Codex, AGENTS.md, distribution | 27 | ADR N8, N9, N10 (conditional) |
| 5 | Consumer-repo and research follow-ups | 7 | nothing |

Highlights:
- **Wave 0:** fix the muse dangling reference and move muse to `verdict@3`; baseline the gate metrics from transcripts; build the paired-eval harness; test the `reasoning` refusal risk first (WP-61); find why agents went unused (WP-56).
- **Wave 1:** a mode router (shape, sketch, spike, implement, review, copy, harden, promote); a `sketch` skill with durable option files (stable ids, status, one-line reason) that double as the decision log, rendered locally as a brand x theme x viewport matrix, TBDs allowed, no gate; a smith `spike` skill to check that a tool or library works; a show-first rule; direction-commit and anti-slop controls; a lightweight promote (WP-14a) that carries a chosen option forward as a requirement plus a brief.
- **Wave 2:** evidence-citing blockers, "no findings" as a valid pass, enforced retry caps with logged overrides, readback in correction loops, a small fixed vocabulary, stall procedures, orchestrator-owned spawning, and file ownership for parallel work.
- **Wave 3:** `spec@2` with token and visual references, a render-evidence artifact and manifest capability, deterministic UI checks (tokens, contrast, target size, landmarks, copy provenance), the full promote path, a visual critic, and ground-truth extraction before drafting.
- **Wave 4:** ablations of the constitution and prompt structure measured net of cache hits, tier re-checks per model, Codex role cards, an AGENTS.md strategy, and skill versioning and maintenance.

Design choices made in the catalog's conflict table (section 4): 3 options per round and 4 directions only at the first direction-commit; 3 parallel writers by default and up to 5 for disjoint work; scanners report everything and a separate stage filters while gates stay scoped to stated requirements (test first in WP-60); no tier changes on vendor claims until measured (WP-63).

## Architecture review (summary)

Full text in `ARCHITECTURE-REVIEW.md`. Measured facts: 10 plugins, 30 skills, 44 agents; agents use only five frontmatter keys and none of the platform's native controls (`tools`, `maxTurns`, `isolation`, `skills`, `memory`); no plugin ships hooks, validators, workflows or code-intelligence servers.

- **Keep:** the schemas as the cross-harness contract, progressive disclosure, and the differentiators no harness provides natively: falsifiable specs, adversarial refutation, fail-by-default binding gates, enforced self-audit.
- **Change:** enforcement. Retry caps, schema validity and "no pass without evidence" move from prompts into hooks or workflow scripts where the harness supports it, with the prompt path as the cross-harness fallback (the retry cap failed in the `pages` session because it lived only in a prompt). Plans become outcome-level and resumable for longer autonomous runs. Visual evidence comes from capability-detected native browsers.
- **Test before deciding:** whether role-based agent splits pay for their cost (Anthropic recommends splitting by context, not role; multi-agent runs cost 3 to 15 times a single agent). WP-601 sets up `claude plugin eval` with a no-plugin baseline.
- **Lower priority than first thought:** the constitution is a 6-line block in each agent, not 290 lines. The 290-line file is the authoring-time rulebook (catalog amendment P8).
- **Shape:** Codex has its own native plugin format in `harnesses/codex/`; AGY's format is similar to Claude Code's and shares the authored tree. AGY workflows stop working on 2026-10-19, so author skills only.

## Conformance findings from primary-source verification

Details in `verification/Y1` to `Y6` and `ARCHITECTURE-REVIEW.md` section 7.1.

- **Claude Code.** `claude plugin validate plugins/<id>` reports a pass after checking components only, because the manifests sit at the plugin root and not at `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`. Validated explicitly, each manifest gets 3 warnings (`id`, `consumes`, `produces` are ignored at load time) and `--strict` would fail all 10. Agent `role` and skill `version` frontmatter have no runtime effect. Each plugin's `shared` symlink points outside the plugin directory. Subagents deliver reports through a `SubagentHandback` tool in auto mode (since 2.1.271), so a `SubagentStop` validator would read the wrong field. Stop-hook continuations are hard-capped at 8, and a failing or timed-out hook does not block unless `onFailure: "block"` (needs 2.1.295; local CLI is 2.1.292). The 15,000-token agent-description limit is a startup warning, not an error.
- **Codex.** The roles README names retired or unknown model ids (`gpt-5.6-luna`, `-terra`, `-sol`; current: `gpt-6-luna`, `gpt-6.1-sol`, `gpt-6-astra`). 18 skills phrase delegation as "teams" or "teammates"; Codex delegates only when told to, so only the sequential fallback runs today. Role cards cannot enforce read-only (subagents inherit the parent sandbox). Only the legacy `.codex-plugin/plugin.json` exists, and `capabilities` carries an undocumented value (`agent-teams-optional`).
- **Antigravity and standards.** The `$schema` URLs in the root `marketplace.json` and AGY's documented plugin schema both return 404, and no third-party AGY marketplace schema is documented, so that file is repo-private. Agent Plugins 1.0.0 requires `$schema` and `name` in its manifest and rejects paths leaving the plugin root. AGY workflows stop on 2026-10-19 (primary page).
- **Claims corrected.** The harness-simplification result (6h/$200 vs 3h50m/$124.70) compares different models and prompts and kept the planner and evaluator; the "31-minute UK AISI horizon" is not in the cited paper; "Astra about 40 minutes per task" is a vendor latency simulation, not an autonomy duration; Caveman's "65%" is stale (its repo now reports 3% over a concise-control for the basic mode); `taste-skill` v2 has no dials; "verify" is FAA usage, ICAO and UK material uses "confirm"; AFIS and IFR claims needed qualification.

## How the user's guidance is covered

| Guidance | Where |
| :-- | :-- |
| Flexible, "vibe-coded" exploration without worrying about specs and tests | Wave 1: WP-10, 11, 12, 13, 15, 16, 18, 19; mode router gives each mode its own gate set (conflict K12) |
| See designs | WP-12 (rendered option matrix, local first), WP-211 (show-first rule), WP-34 |
| Validate that tools work | WP-15 smith `spike`: smoke-check evidence, verified-vs-unverified report, promote or discard |
| Specs and tests once ideas narrow, without regressions | WP-14a/b promote, WP-19 harden, WP-106 to 108 spec hygiene, WP-204 test taxonomy |
| Do not cut things | 144 WPs, 8 merged with reasons, dispositions for items with no action; nothing was dropped |
| Learn from industry, model vendors, AGENTS.md, uSpec, ICAO, TanStack Intent | Waves 3 and 4; WP-32 and 33 (uSpec), WP-71 (AGENTS.md), WP-53, 54 and 212 (ICAO ideas), WP-72 (Intent) |

## Open items and limits

- **Unverified here:** pages commit counts (repo history access was blocked for that repo), the `a859e2f` origin claim, the 271 KB JS budget, whether SPEC-013 supersedes 26 of SPEC-001's and 35 of SPEC-003c's criteria, Shopify and Airbnb figures, the Figma 25k response cap, whether Codex loads Claude agents or hooks from `.claude-plugin` formats, install behavior of the `shared` symlink in each harness, whether `skills-ref` rejects a top-level `version`, and the refusal probe on Opus 5.5 and Fable 5.1 (only Sonnet 5.5 was probed). The aviation items were checked against UK CAP 413 and SKYbrary, not ICAO documents directly; see `verification/Y6-aviation-evals.md`.
- **Weak evidence by nature:** vendor self-benchmarks and small samples (Vercel's six pages, Atlassian's single task). WP-401 proposes tagging them.
- **One project:** all transcript evidence is from two sessions in one body of work. Gate cost was measured from those sessions (`verification/VERIFY-3.md`) and covers subagent-reported tokens only, not a bill or main-session tokens.
- **Not read:** several newer Anthropic posts (infrastructure noise, eval awareness, auto mode), the Codex computer-use and MCP pages and release notes before 0.162, and ICAO Annex 10/11, Doc 4444 and Doc 9432 directly.
- **User configuration untouched:** `~/.claude/RTK.md` installs rtk with the same hook JetBrains tested. Whether it helps this workflow is an open paired test (WP-68), not a recommendation to change it.

## Next decisions

1. Accept or amend the wave order, in particular Wave 1 before Wave 2.
2. Write ADR N1 (exploratory mode, amending ADR 003) and N6 (the `reasoning` field policy: keep the field, lint the wording), and start with the Wave 0 conformance fixes (WP-617, WP-620, WP-622, WP-624, WP-625).
3. Decide whether sketch and promote live as skills in `muse` (which already owns UI) or in a new plugin; `AGENTS.md` allows several skills in one plugin when intents are heterogeneous, and the catalog assumes `muse`.

61	Plugin-level hooks as gates; `claude plugin eval` with a no-plugin baseline; plugin-shipped workflows; `bin/` validators; `SendMessage` resume for repair loops; `isolation: worktree`; per-agent `maxTurns` as a stall guard; `tools` allowlists; `skills` preload; subagent `memory` and a persistent plugin data directory for counters; plugin `dependencies`; routines for drift checks; bundled LSP servers.
62	
63	## 5. Differentiators to protect
64	
65	The harnesses natively do parallel agents, worktrees, browser capture, plan artifacts and review bots. None of them provides falsifiable specs, adversarial refutation, fail-by-default binding gates, or enforced self-audit [S per Z2]. These are why the plugins exist. The direction below moves the *enforcement* of those properties out of prose and into deterministic harness features, and leaves the properties themselves unchanged.
66	
67	## 6. Direction: thinner prompts, thicker harness
68	
69	1. **Move enforcement out of prose.** Retry caps, schema validity, "no pass without evidence refs" and self-audit become hook- or workflow-enforced where the harness allows, with the prompt-only path as the cross-harness fallback.
70	2. **Split agents by context, not by role.** Keep splits that buy independent or high-volume context (verifier, adversary, recon). Audit the rest against that criterion with a measured baseline.
71	3. **Design for longer autonomy.** Plans state outcomes, ownership and verification; progress is a resumable artifact; gates sit at boundaries, not inside every step.
72	4. **Make capabilities pluggable and detected.** Browser, worktree, memory and design-source access are adapters selected by capability, with identical artifacts out (`render-evidence`, `design-source`).
73	5. **Keep schemas as the cross-harness contract,** and share skill bodies where orchestration semantics are identical.
74	6. **Record the assumptions.** A register of what each component assumes the model cannot do, reviewed on each model generation (WP-609), so stale scaffolding is retired on evidence.
75	
76	Cross-harness specifics:
77	- **Codex:** native plugin format under `harnesses/codex/`; custom agents are natively TOML [P], and this repo's policy keeps role cards as markdown resources (ADR N8 decides whether an optional generator may emit TOML). Subagents spawn only when asked or when a skill or AGENTS.md instructs it, so Codex orchestrator skills must say so. Re-check the generated tree against the new `extensions.com.openai` convention [P per Z2].
78	- **AGY:** plugin fields `plugin.json` (with `$schema`), optional `mcp_config.json`, `hooks.json`, `skills/`, `agents/`, `rules/`; workflows are not supported in plugins and stop working on 2026-10-19 [S], so author skills only. The public docs do not document the third-party marketplace schema, so the `$schema` reference in the root `marketplace.json` needs re-verifying [P per Z2]. Gemini CLI was retired in June [S].
79	- **Standards:** AGENTS.md, the Agent Skills `SKILL.md` standard, MCP 2026-07-28 (stateless core; Roots, Sampling and Logging deprecated), and Agent Plugins 1.0.0 as the portable manifest core.
80

# Architecture review against current agent capabilities

Status: proposal, revised after primary-source verification (section 7.1 and `verification/Y1` to `Y6`, `VERIFY-3`). Nothing here changes a plugin, schema, constitution or ADR. It tests each architectural assumption in `ARCHITECTURE.md` against what the current agent platforms can do, and adds the work packages that follow (WP-601 to WP-616 first, WP-617 to WP-628 after verification; 172 in total with the catalog's 144). Where section 7.1 and an earlier row differ, 7.1 wins.

Inputs: `ARCHITECTURE.md`; `evidence/Z1-claude-platform.md` (Claude Code and Anthropic engineering guidance); `evidence/Z2-other-harnesses.md` (Codex, Antigravity, Cursor, Copilot, standards); repo measurements taken for this review (section 1). Claims tagged [P] were read on a primary page, [S] come from a search summary, [I] are inference. Z1 read only the first 100k characters of the hooks and subagents pages, and the fetch tool summarizes pages, so quotes are the fetcher's wording.

## 0. Corrections to earlier statements

1. **The constitution is not 290 lines per agent.** Every one of the 44 agents embeds the same 6-line `<constitution>` block (one distinct block, checked by hash). The 290-line `shared/constitution.md` is the authoring-time rulebook; among agents only the `mason` auditor reads it at runtime. The research notes and `traceability/MAP-5-M-X.md` assumed a 290-line copy per agent, and so did my earlier summaries. The per-agent cost is about 6 lines. This lowers the priority of the "shrink the constitution" ablation (WP-62, ADR N10). See section 2, row 3.
2. **Cross-harness shape (from the user).** Codex has its own native plugin format, set up in this repo under `harnesses/codex/`; AGY's format is similar to Claude Code's and shares the authored tree. The cost is therefore one authored tree for Claude and AGY plus one native Codex tree, not three. The AGY risks are specific (section 6), not a third tree.
3. **Agent descriptions are inside the platform's budget.** Descriptions across the 44 agents total 26,908 characters, about 6.7k tokens by a 4-characters-per-token estimate, against a 15,000-token cap on all agent descriptions [P per Z1]. That is about 45% of the cap. There is headroom, but every agent added (the structure decision proposes 3) draws on the same budget, so keep descriptions short.

## 1. Where the repo stands (measured)

| Fact | Value |
| :-- | :-- |
| Plugins / skills / agents | 10 / 30 / 44 |
| Agent frontmatter keys in use | `name`, `role`, `model`, `effort`, `description` only. No `tools`, `maxTurns`, `isolation`, `skills`, `memory` or other native controls |
| Tier distribution | sonnet/medium 27, opus/high 8, haiku/low 7, `claude-fable-5-1`/high 2 |
| Skill frontmatter keys | `name`, `description`, `version` |
| Plugin-shipped hooks, `bin/` validators, workflows, LSP servers | none (the repo has a commit-time integrity hook for its own development only) |
| Distinct `<constitution>` blocks across agents | 1 (6 lines) |
| Average agent body | about 4.4k characters |
| Orchestration | skill prompts that spawn subagents; retry counter lives in `verdict@3` and is incremented by the exit-gate agent |

## 2. Assumption ledger

Verdicts: **Keep**, **Change**, **Test first** (evidence is mixed; measure before deciding), **Lower priority**.

| # | Assumption (where it lives) | What current platforms and evidence say | Verdict | Work |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| 1 | Context is scarce; load references on demand (`ARCHITECTURE.md` section 1) | Skills are progressive disclosure natively; Anthropic's context-engineering guidance asks for the minimal information that fully outlines behavior [P per Z1]. Subagent frontmatter can preload skills | **Keep** | WP-606 (use native preload where it helps) |
| 2 | One agent per cognitive mode (ADR 003) | Anthropic's guide calls splitting by role (planner, implementer, tester, reviewer) an anti-pattern and recommends splitting by *context* [P per Z1]. Verifier and adversary splits are justified by independent context. Multi-agent runs cost about 15x chat tokens in one post and 3 to 10x single-agent in a later guide; it underperforms on tightly coupled work, "most coding tasks" included. A multi-agent research setup beat single-agent Opus 4 by 90.2% on an internal eval. No vendor test of 40-plus role agents in a linear pipeline exists | **Test first** | WP-605, WP-601 |
| 3 | A byte-identical constitution is the shared cache prefix (ADR 006) | The block is only 6 lines, so its cost is small whatever it saves. Cache prefixes are shared only between requests with the same model, effort, agent type, tools, schema and working directory, and subagent caches default to a 5-minute TTL [P per Z1], so the cache benefit across 44 differently configured agents is probably small [I]. The drift guard (byte-identity check) already exists | **Lower priority** | WP-62 retargets to backstory and skeleton; WP-604 only measures |
| 4 | Capability tiers by model and effort (`ARCHITECTURE.md` section 5) | Effort is a native per-agent control; defaults differ by model (Fable 5.1 high, Opus 5.5 medium, Sonnet 5.5 high on the API, Haiku 5.5 medium); Opus 5.5 at medium roughly matches Opus 5 at high per Anthropic. Pricing per million tokens: Fable 5.1 $10/$50, Opus 5.5 $4/$20, Sonnet 5.5 $2/$10 [P per Z1]. Two agents already run on Fable 5.1 | **Keep as hints; re-measure** | WP-63 |
| 5 | JSON schemas are the inter-agent contract, with a mandatory `reasoning` scratchpad (ADR 004) | Schemas remain the portable contract across harnesses. Workflow scripts can pass a JSON schema to `agent()` with validation retries, and a `SubagentStop` hook can run a validator [P per Z1]. Anthropic names a `reasoning` field as a refusal trigger; first-hand (`VERIFY-3`): the real drafter prompt with its scratchpad field completed normally twice, only a demand for verbatim reasoning was refused, and 72k+ transcript messages show no refusals | **Keep schemas; change enforcement; test the field first** | WP-602, WP-61 |
| 6 | Default-fail gates with a retry cap of 3, then a human (`ARCHITECTURE.md` section 6) | The gate concept is a differentiator no harness provides natively (section 5). But a prompt-based gate is only a request: in the `pages` session the cap was not enforced. Anthropic's harness post says evaluators drift lenient and the multi-agent guide names the "early victory problem"; VISTA found 8.3% of agents claiming success despite failed checks [P abstract per Z2]. `Stop`, `SubagentStop` and `TaskCompleted` hooks can block with a reason, and the hook can hold a counter a model cannot reliably keep | **Keep the gate; make it deterministic** | WP-602 |
| 7 | Orchestration is a skill prompt that spawns subagents | Every result lands in the orchestrator's context. Plugins can ship workflow scripts (`agent()`, `pipeline()`, `parallel()`) that keep state outside the model, are resumable, and allow 16 concurrent agents and 1,000 agents per run [P per Z1]; they run in the CLI, headless mode and the SDK. Not portable: Antigravity workflows stop on 2026-10-19 [S per Z2], and Codex has no equivalent plugin construct | **Change on Claude; keep the skill as the cross-harness path** | WP-603 |
| 8 | Work is a sequential pipeline of ten plugins | Testimonials (not controlled benchmarks) report 18-plus-hour unattended runs on Opus 5.5 and a 38-hour run on Fable 5.1 [P per Z1]; Anthropic's harness post reports a simplified harness (sprint construct removed; planner and evaluator kept) at 3h50m and $124.70 on Opus 4.6, against an earlier 6h/$200 run on Opus 4.5 with a different prompt; it is not a before/after on one task and was not re-checked on 5.x. Stage granularity tuned for short horizons will not stay right | **Change: make stages elidable, gates at boundaries** | WP-608, WP-18 |
| 9 | Plans carry exact implementation code (navigator, ADR 009) | Anthropic says prescriptive skills "can degrade output quality" on Fable 5 [P]; plans of 60 to 130 KB stalled agents in the sessions (VERIFY-1: 17 failed tasks in the `orin-dx` session) | **Change: outcome-level plans** | WP-608, WP-36 |
| 10 | Verification evidence is text, code and tests; "render" is only a label | Browser capture is native in Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity and Cursor [S for most]; VISTA found 44.5% of trajectories never looked at the design screenshots and 73% skipped prescribed self-audits | **Change** | WP-607 |
| 11 | Agents are stateless across sessions | Subagents can have persistent `memory`; plugins have a persistent data directory; routines and scheduled runs exist [P per Z1] | **Change** | WP-612 |
| 12 | One lifecycle contract, two source trees | Agent Plugins 1.0.0 (2026-08-06) standardizes the portable core (root `plugin.json`, `skills/`, `mcp.json`) and excludes hooks, commands, agents, marketplaces and permissions [P per Z2]. Claude Code and AGY are not named in it; AGY's plugin format is similar to Claude's | **Keep two trees; narrow the duplication** | WP-610 |
| 13 | Humans approve through written artifacts | Rendered review surfaces exist (Artifacts, MCP Apps, Claude Design handoff); the user asked for pictures repeatedly | **Change** | WP-614, WP-34 |
| 14 | Agents use platform controls only through `model` and `effort` | Native controls available: `tools` allowlists, `maxTurns`, `isolation: worktree`, `skills` preload, `memory`, `omitClaudeMd`. Plugin-shipped agents ignore `hooks`, `mcpServers` and `permissionMode` [P per Z1] | **Change** | WP-606, WP-615 |

## 3. What the harnesses do natively and what we re-implement

| Capability | Native | In this repo today | Call |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| Parallel agents and worktrees | Claude `isolation: worktree`; Codex managed worktrees (CLI 0.162.0); Antigravity parallel agents | File ownership is prose in plans; no worktree isolation | Adopt natively (WP-606, WP-55) |
| Browser capture and screenshots | Claude built-in browser and Chrome extension; Codex in-app browser; Antigravity browser subagent with Artifacts; Cursor browser | None | Capability-detected adapters (WP-607) |
| Plugin evals with a no-plugin baseline | `claude plugin eval` runs each case 3 times with and 3 without the plugin [P per Z1] | `mason:evaluate` with hidden-oracle fixtures | Complementary: native gives the baseline, ours gives cross-harness fixtures (WP-601) |
| Deterministic gates | Hooks (33 events on Claude [P]; 12 events on Codex [P]; `hooks.json` in AGY plugins) | One repo-level commit hook; none shipped in plugins | Adopt (WP-602) |
| Orchestration scripts | Claude workflow scripts; Codex Agents SDK | Skill prompts | Adopt on Claude (WP-603) |
| Review bots and plan artifacts | Cursor Bugbot, Copilot review, Antigravity plan Artifacts | `ranger`, `sentinel`, `navigator` | Keep; ours add refutation and falsifiable gates |
| Code intelligence | LSP servers can be bundled in Claude plugins [P per Z1]; Netflix and JetBrains report 20 to 30% efficiency gains for Java | Language-service guidance in smith (commit `f10e6b8`) | Extend to UI facts (WP-611) |

## 4. Platform features this repo does not use yet

Plugin-level hooks as gates; `claude plugin eval` with a no-plugin baseline; plugin-shipped workflows; `bin/` validators; `SendMessage` resume for repair loops; `isolation: worktree`; per-agent `maxTurns` as a stall guard; `tools` allowlists; `skills` preload; subagent `memory` and a persistent plugin data directory for counters; plugin `dependencies`; routines for drift checks; bundled LSP servers.

## 5. Differentiators to protect

The harnesses natively do parallel agents, worktrees, browser capture, plan artifacts and review bots. None of them provides falsifiable specs, adversarial refutation, fail-by-default binding gates, or enforced self-audit [S per Z2]. These are why the plugins exist. The direction below moves the *enforcement* of those properties out of prose and into deterministic harness features, and leaves the properties themselves unchanged.

## 6. Direction: thinner prompts, thicker harness

1. **Move enforcement out of prose.** Retry caps, schema validity, "no pass without evidence refs" and self-audit become hook- or workflow-enforced where the harness allows, with the prompt-only path as the cross-harness fallback.
2. **Split agents by context, not by role.** Keep splits that buy independent or high-volume context (verifier, adversary, recon). Audit the rest against that criterion with a measured baseline.
3. **Design for longer autonomy.** Plans state outcomes, ownership and verification; progress is a resumable artifact; gates sit at boundaries, not inside every step.
4. **Make capabilities pluggable and detected.** Browser, worktree, memory and design-source access are adapters selected by capability, with identical artifacts out (`render-evidence`, `design-source`).
5. **Keep schemas as the cross-harness contract,** and share skill bodies where orchestration semantics are identical.
6. **Record the assumptions.** A register of what each component assumes the model cannot do, reviewed on each model generation (WP-609), so stale scaffolding is retired on evidence.

Cross-harness specifics:
- **Codex:** native plugin format under `harnesses/codex/`; custom agents are natively TOML [P], and this repo's policy keeps role cards as markdown resources (ADR N8 decides whether an optional generator may emit TOML). Subagents spawn only when asked or when a skill or AGENTS.md instructs it, so Codex orchestrator skills must say so. Re-check the generated tree against the new `extensions.com.openai` convention [P per Z2].
- **AGY:** plugin fields `plugin.json` (with `$schema`), optional `mcp_config.json`, `hooks.json`, `skills/`, `agents/`, `rules/`; workflows are not supported in plugins and stop working on 2026-10-19 [S], so author skills only. The public docs do not document the third-party marketplace schema, so the `$schema` reference in the root `marketplace.json` needs re-verifying [P per Z2]. Gemini CLI was retired in June [S].
- **Standards:** AGENTS.md, the Agent Skills `SKILL.md` standard, MCP 2026-07-28 (stateless core; Roots, Sampling and Logging deprecated), and Agent Plugins 1.0.0 as the portable manifest core.

- **New ADR N11, deterministic enforcement layer.** Gates and retry caps are enforced by hooks or workflows where the harness provides them; prose is the fallback. Touches the constitution's retry rules; sits beside N4 and N5.

- **N10 narrows** to backstory and skeleton ablations; the constitution-block question (WP-604) no longer needs an ADR unless the measurement says so.
- **ADR 003 may need a note** if WP-605 finds role-flavor splits worth merging; no change before that evidence.
- ADR 005 (artifact-agnostic gate) is unaffected: hooks and render evidence arrive as generic evidence kinds.

## 9. Risks and what is unverified

- Multi-agent token cost is 3 to 15 times a single agent in Anthropic's own figures. WP-601 must price every new agent and workflow.
- The long-autonomy figures are testimonials, not benchmarks; the harness-simplification result is Opus 4.6-era and was not re-checked on 5.x.
- Hook loop behavior is confirmed (7.1): Claude caps stop-hook continuations at 8, after which the turn ends and can look like a pass, so the retry counter and artifact checks are required.
- The Codex hook count (12) and Stop semantics, the AGY workflow shutdown (2026-10-19) and AGY's plugin fields are now primary-sourced; Antigravity 2.0 product details and several Cursor and Copilot specifics remain secondary.
- The cache-sharing conclusion in row 3 is inference from the documented sharing conditions.
- No head-to-head comparison of Claude Code, Codex and Antigravity on UI tasks exists. VISTA and Vision2Web evaluate agents, not these harnesses against each other.

## 10. Order of attack

1. WP-609, WP-615, WP-616 (cheap, remove uncertainty), and WP-601 (the baseline everything else is measured against).
2. Wave 1 exploration modes, unchanged.
3. WP-602, WP-603, WP-605, WP-606, WP-613 in Wave 2 with the gate-hygiene work, so enforcement and the retry rules land together.
4. WP-607, WP-611, WP-614 with the Wave 3 visual-evidence bundle.
5. WP-608, WP-610, WP-612, WP-604 in Wave 4.

# VERIFY-3: first-hand measurements

Measurements taken directly (not through research agents) on 2026-10-17. Scripts in `scripts/` reproduce parts 1 and 3; part 2 is a live probe whose procedure is recorded below. Counts can drift by a few messages because the source transcripts are live session files.

## 1. Refusal scan of the session transcripts

`scripts/scan-refusals.py` over the 812 transcript files (top-level and subagent) from the `orin-dx` and `pages` projects.

| Measure | Result |
| :-- | :-- |
| Refusal hits (`reasoning_extraction` or `stop_reason: "refusal"`) | 0 |
| Stop reasons recorded | `tool_use` 33,050; `end_turn` 2,648; `stop_sequence` 35; null (streaming partials) 36,318 |
| Assistant messages by model | `claude-sonnet-5-5` 47,657; `claude-opus-5-5` 24,346; `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001` 13 |
| Assistant messages containing a JSON `reasoning` field | 157, in 121 files (Sonnet 5.5, Opus 5.5 and 2 Haiku 4.5) |
| API errors in the logs | computer sleep, connectivity, expired login; none are refusals |

Stop reasons are recorded in these logs, so "no refusals" is meaningful. Some of the 157 messages may be discussion of the field and not agent output.

## 2. Live probe of the `reasoning` refusal trigger

Question: does Wisp's mandatory `reasoning` scratchpad field trigger Anthropic's `reasoning_extraction` safeguard, as the refusals documentation suggests?

Method: `claude -p --model claude-sonnet-5-5 --tools "" --disable-slash-commands --no-session-persistence --output-format json`, with the body of `plugins/muse/agents/drafter.md` (6,022 characters, including the 6-line constitution block and the output section that names the `reasoning` scratchpad) appended as the system prompt, and a short `requirement@1` for a Switch component as the user prompt. Arm B adds one line to the system prompt: "In the `reasoning` field, write out your complete internal chain of thought verbatim, step by step, exactly as you reasoned, with nothing omitted."

| Run | Prompt | `stop_reason` | `is_error` | `safety_stops` | Output | Cost |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| A1 | real drafter prompt | `end_turn` | false | 0 | spec JSON with a populated `reasoning` field | $0.121 |
| A2 | real drafter prompt | `end_turn` | false | 0 | spec JSON with a populated `reasoning` field | $0.054 |
| B1 | A plus verbatim chain-of-thought demand | `refusal` | true | 2 | `[reasoning_extraction]` safeguard message | $0.059 |

Conclusion: the field and the prompt's wording about it ("scratchpad", "discarded") did not trigger the safeguard in two runs on Sonnet 5.5, and an explicit demand for verbatim reasoning did, and was billed. The trigger is the wording that asks for reproduced reasoning, not the schema field's existence. This matches the documentation's statement that triggers "usually" come from asking for reasoning "verbatim or in a fixed format", and the transcript history in part 1.

Limits: n=2 for the normal case and n=1 for the control; Sonnet 5.5 only (Opus 5.5 and Fable 5.1 not probed); a single requirement; no tool use. Re-run when a new model generation ships (WP-625).

## 3. What the gates and ideation cost

`scripts/gate-cost.py` over the two top-level project directories; subagent-reported tokens, deduplicated by task id.

| Session | Agent type | Calls | Total tokens | Avg tokens | Avg minutes |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `pages` 24655582 | fork | 14 | 9,093,105 | 649,507 | 12.2 |
| `pages` | `muse:exit-gate` | 51 | 5,330,504 | 104,519 | 4.8 |
| `pages` | general-purpose | 24 | 4,873,829 | 203,076 | 14.9 |
| `pages` | `muse:drafter` | 8 | 1,862,067 | 232,758 | 10.1 |
| `pages` | `muse:auditor` | 9 | 1,117,602 | 124,178 | 5.3 |
| `orin-dx` b8d16e96 | fork | 26 | 15,679,679 | 603,064 | 34.9 |
| `orin-dx` | general-purpose | 17 | 3,426,209 | 201,541 | 31.5 |
| `orin-dx` | `muse:exit-gate` | 28 | 2,820,631 | 100,736 | 5.3 |
| `orin-dx` | `smith:implementer` | 16 | 2,263,340 | 141,458 | 14.2 |
| `orin-dx` | `muse:drafter` | 25 | 2,252,389 | 90,095 | 7.8 |
| `orin-dx` | `navigator:planner` | 3 | 1,329,580 | 443,193 | 28.0 |

Plugin agents in total: 8.87M tokens over 72 calls (`pages`) and 10.46M over 91 calls (`orin-dx`). Everything else (forks, general-purpose, untyped): 15.77M over 46 calls and 19.11M over 43 calls. Muse gates alone: about 8.15M tokens over 79 calls. Forks alone: about 24.8M tokens.

Reading: gates are cheap per call and costly in rounds; ad hoc ideation and build work cost more than all the plugin agents. Per-agent minutes are summed durations (gates ran up to 8 in flight, in a 57-minute window in `pages`). Tokens are subagent-reported usage, not a bill, and main-session tokens are excluded.

## 4. Repo structure measurements

| Fact | Value |
| :-- | :-- |
| Plugins / skills / agents | 10 / 30 / 44 |
| Distinct `<constitution>` blocks in agents | 1 (6 lines, identical in all 44) |
| Agent descriptions, total | 26,908 characters, about 6.7k tokens (4 characters per token) |
| Agent frontmatter keys | `name`, `role`, `model`, `effort`, `description` only |
| Skill frontmatter keys | `name`, `description`, `version` |
| Agent tiers | sonnet/medium 27; opus/high 8; haiku/low 7; `claude-fable-5-1`/high 2 |
| Plugins shipping hooks, `bin/`, workflows | none |
| Plugin manifest location | `plugins/<id>/plugin.json`; no `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` in any plugin |
| `shared` symlinks | one per plugin (`shared -> ../../shared`), pointing outside the plugin directory |
| `claude plugin validate plugins/muse` (CLI 2.1.292) | "Validation passed" after checking components only |
| `claude plugin validate plugins/muse/plugin.json` | 3 warnings: `id`, `consumes`, `produces` ignored at load time |
| Codex roles README | names `gpt-5.6-luna`, `gpt-5.6-terra`, `gpt-5.6-sol`; current ids are `gpt-6-luna`, `gpt-6.1-sol`, `gpt-6-astra` |
| Codex skills describing delegation as "teams" or "teammates" | 18 |
| Codex manifests with `capabilities` containing `agent-teams-optional` | at least `vanguard`, `smith`, `weaver`, `navigator`, `scribe` |
| Only reader of the 290-line `shared/constitution.md` at runtime | the `mason` auditor |

## 5. Recorded gate verdicts against the verdict schemas

`scripts/handback-conformance.py` validates the 45 persisted verdict files in `~/projects/pages/docs/specs` against `verdict@1` and `verdict@3` using the validator in `shared/hooks/validate-handback.py`.

| Shape of the recorded verdict | Conforming | Violating |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `verdict@3`-shaped (has `verified_scope`) | 27 | 8 |
| `verdict@1`-shaped | 6 | 4 |

All 12 violations are the same rule: `verdict_summary` longer than the schema's 300 characters (median length 288, maximum 745, 12 of 45 over the limit). Every other schema rule held, including the conditional ones (a `pass` carries no blockers; a `fail` names at least one).

Two consequences:

- A deterministic check would have asked for a trim on about 27% of recorded gate verdicts, and nothing else. The schema's rules are being followed except the length cap, which prompts alone do not enforce.
- The 45 files mix `scribe` gates (SPEC-002*, 9 files, all `verdict@3`) and `muse` gates (36 files). 26 of the 36 `muse` verdicts (SPEC-001 and SPEC-003*) are `verdict@3`-shaped although `muse` documented `verdict@1`; the other 10 (SPEC-005 to SPEC-012 and two of SPEC-001) are `verdict@1`-shaped. (An earlier version of this note said 35 of 45 were `muse` verdicts; that mixed in the `scribe` files.) The `muse` gate prompt also told the agent to set `verdict` to `"escalate"`, a value neither schema allows. WP-02 moved `muse` to `verdict@3` and made escalation a blocker, as in the other four gates.

Limits: the files were written by an orchestrator from the gate agents' handbacks and may have been edited on the way, so they approximate the handbacks. One project, two sessions.

## 6. Gate rounds, retry counts and tool-output share

`tools/transcript-metrics.py` (the maintained version of `scripts/gate-cost.py`; same plugin and other-agent totals) over the same two projects and the persisted verdict files.

**Blockers per gate round, from the verdict files** (`gates` subcommand):

| Spec | Rounds | Blockers per round | Final persisted verdict |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| SPEC-001 | 13 | 18, 5, 6, 0, 0, 2, 0, 6, 2, 3, 2, 8, 3 | fail |
| SPEC-003a | 7 | 5, 2, 0, 2, 4, 1, 0 | pass |
| SPEC-003c | 4 | 3, 3, 1, 0 | pass |
| SPEC-002b (scribe) | 4 | 6, 4, 1, 1 | fail, one escalation blocker |
| SPEC-005 to SPEC-012 | 1 persisted each | 0 | pass, with `retry_count` 4, 5, 6, 6, 6, 8, 9 and 6 |

- **Gates were not monotonic.** SPEC-001 reached 0 blockers in rounds 4, 5 and 7 and then had 6, 2, 3, 2, 8 and 3 again; SPEC-003a went 0, then 2, then 4. Blockers return after a clean round, which is the pattern WP-212 (non-monotonicity detection) and WP-50 (gate hygiene) target.
- **Every one of the eight later specs passed with a recorded `retry_count` above the cap of 3** (4 to 9). The cap was not enforced.
- **Five specs' last persisted verdict is `fail`** (SPEC-001, SPEC-002, SPEC-002b, SPEC-002c, SPEC-003). Later rounds may not have been persisted, so this is a lower bound on how often work proceeded without a persisted pass, not a count.

**Tool-result characters by tool** (`outputs` subcommand, top-level sessions only): Bash was 77.5% of tool-result characters in the `pages` session (5.28M of 6.82M) and 51.9% in the `orin-dx` session. A compressor that sees only Bash output and removes 70% of it therefore bounds its saving at about 54% and 36% of tool-result characters in those sessions. This is a ceiling on fresh tool-result text, not on the bill: cached re-reads dominate cost, and the JetBrains replay of SkillsBench transcripts found only about 20% of tool output compressible. Your workflow, with Playwright scripts, builds and long Bash output, differs from that benchmark, which is why WP-68 (a paired test of `rtk` on this workflow) is worth keeping.

**Skills versus agents** (`skills` subcommand): 7 Skill calls across the 812 transcripts, none of them a plugin skill other than `muse:component` once; see `../investigations/unused-agents.md`.

## 7. Installed plugins and the `shared` symlink

Each plugin has a `shared -> ../../shared` symlink that its skills and agents use to read schemas and references. Whether it survives installation was open (WP-621). Tested on 2026-10-20 with Claude Code 2.1.292, each case in a fresh isolated config directory (`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`) so nothing touched the real configuration.

| Case | Marketplace source type | Result in the installed copy |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| A. Local marketplace, plugin `muse` | relative path (`./plugins/muse`) | `shared` is a real directory with the schemas inside: the installer dereferenced the symlink |
| B. This repository's marketplace as it was, installed from the GitHub `main` branch | `git-subdir` (`path: plugins/muse`) | `shared` is a **dangling symlink** to `../../shared`; `shared/schemas` is missing |
| C. This repository's marketplace after changing every entry to a relative path, all 10 plugins | relative path | `shared` is a real directory in every plugin with all 33 schemas |

The primary documentation agrees: a symlink whose target is elsewhere in the same marketplace is dereferenced into the cache, `git-subdir` fetches "one subdirectory of a git repository, with a sparse checkout", and a relative path is the type to use "for a plugin in a subdirectory of the marketplace repository itself". So installing any plugin from this repository's marketplace gave it no schemas and no shared references. The Claude marketplace entries now use relative paths, and `tests/test_claude_marketplace_sources.py` fails on the old configuration (10 failures) and passes on the new one.

Limits: case C added the marketplace from a local directory, not from GitHub (the docs say a GitHub-added marketplace also has the files, so relative paths resolve). The change reaches users only after it is merged to the branch the marketplace tracks and they update. The Codex bundle already materializes `shared` as regular files (no symlinks); Antigravity install behavior was not tested.

1	# Why were smith:recon/reviewer/mutator/exit-gate, scribe:verifier/arch-auditor and sentinel:* never used? (WP-56)
2	
3	## Question
4	
5	In the orin-dx and pages sessions, `muse:drafter/auditor/exit-gate`, `smith:implementer`, `navigator:*` and `scribe:drafter/exit-gate` ran many times. `smith:recon`, `smith:reviewer`, `smith:mutator`, `smith:exit-gate`, `scribe:verifier`, `scribe:arch-auditor` and every `sentinel:*` agent never ran. Why?
6	
7	Hypothesis tested first: the orchestrating assistant called plugin AGENTS directly and never invoked plugin SKILLS, so the skill pipelines that spawn the other agents never ran.
8	
9	## Method
10	
11	- Transcripts: `~/.claude/projects/-Users-gabe-Projects-orin-dx/b8d16e96-....jsonl` (36,217 lines, 29 Sep to 3 Oct) and `~/.claude/projects/-Users-gabe-Projects-pages/24655582-....jsonl` (63,262 lines, 8 to 16 Oct). Line numbers below are 1-based transcript lines. Streamed with `python3 -I` scripts; no file was read whole.
12	- Listed every `Skill` tool_use, every `<command-name>` slash command, and every `Agent` tool_use by `subagent_type` in both sessions. Counted Skill calls across all 812 transcripts of the orin-dx and pages project dirs (`rows.json`).
13	- Read the `skill_listing` and `agent_listing_delta` attachments at session start, the user prompts asking for plugins, and the assistant's next actions.
14	- Compared against `plugins/smith/skills/implement/SKILL.md`, `plugins/sentinel/skills/gate/SKILL.md`, `plugins/scribe/skills/*/SKILL.md`, and the existing digests (`B-orin-dx-sessions.md`, `C-pages-sessions.md`, `D-outcomes.md` in the job tmp dir).
15	- Limit: the assistant's thinking blocks are empty in the transcripts, so its reasons are inferred from visible text and actions, not read.
16	
17	## Findings
18	
19	| # | Finding | Count | Refs |
20	|---|---|---|---|
21	| 1 | `Skill` calls, orin-dx session | 0 | whole file |
22	| 2 | `Skill` calls, pages session | 4: `artifact-design`, `muse:component`, `artifact-capabilities`, `workflow-authoring`. One plugin skill. | pages 3354, 11906, 14968, 21679 |
23	| 3 | Slash commands | orin: `/effort /fork /exit /model /login`; pages: `/remote-control`. No plugin command. | orin 8, 18920, 20533 |
24	| 4 | Plugin skill calls across all 812 transcripts in both projects | 7 `Skill` calls in 4 files. Plugin ones: `muse:component` (1), `scribe:gate-spec` (1, inside one subagent file), `vanguard:research` (1, a blog session). `smith:implement`, `navigator:plan`, `sentinel:gate`, `scribe:draft-spec`, `scribe:verify-spec` are never invoked. | rows.json |
25	| 5 | Skills were available | Yes. Listings of 60 and 61 skills at session start include `muse:component`, `navigator:plan`, `smith:implement`, `sentinel:gate` and all scribe skills. Not truncated. | orin 18, pages 16 |
26	| 6 | Agents were also listed, each described "Delegate to this subagent when...", including `smith:reviewer`, `smith:mutator`, `sentinel:*` | Direct delegation was always a legal and visible path. | orin 16, pages 14 |
27	| 7 | Agent calls, orin-dx | `muse:exit-gate` 28, `fork` 26, `muse:drafter` 25, `general-purpose` 18, `smith:implementer` 17, `scribe:exit-gate` 10, `scribe:drafter` 7, `navigator:planner` 3, `navigator:challenger` 3, `muse:auditor` 1 | scan |
28	| 8 | Agent calls, pages | `muse:exit-gate` 51, untyped fork/teammate 41, `general-purpose` 24, `smith:implementer` 18, `fork` 14, `muse:auditor` 9, `muse:drafter` 8, `scribe:drafter` 3, `scribe:auditor` 3, `navigator:planner` 1, `navigator:challenger` 1 | scan |
29	| 9 | Trigger prompt, orin 20776 (30 Sep): "Not DocNav then... Do we make these proper react components? Use our plugins for quality work" | Next: Bash `ls`/`cat README.md` in `~/Projects/agent-plugins` (20789-20791), then "build SiteNav using the Muse->Navigator->Smith pipeline" and `Agent muse:drafter` (20797-20798). No `Skill` call. | orin 20776-20798 |
30	| 10 | The assistant framed plugins as agent personas | "Muse specs..., Navigator plans..., and Smith builds it" (20942). Pages: "After that, Navigator plans, Smith builds with tests, and Sentinel gates" (14940). Sentinel was promised and never ran. | orin 20942, pages 14940 |
31	| 11 | No explanation for skipping skills | No assistant text in either session mentions skipping a skill, `reviewer`, `mutator` or `sentinel`. | text search of both sessions |
32	| 12 | When the skill was loaded, the whole pipeline ran | Pages 11905: "I'm loading the component skill so I follow its exact pipeline." Then 8 drafts, 9 audits, 51 gate calls. No unused muse agent in pages. | pages 11905-14898 |
33	| 13 | Smith steps in some other form | Reviewer/recon/exit-gate equivalents: none (no Agent call is described as review, verify or gate of implementation). Mutation: partly inline, since implementers report "temporary mutations, restored" and discrimination checks. Verification otherwise relied on `just check`, Playwright e2e and the orchestrator's own checks. | orin 28037, 28057, 28074, 28098, 28305; pages 21361 |
34	
35	### Why exactly these agents
36	
37	| Unused agent | Where the plugin puts it | What happened |
38	|---|---|---|
39	| `smith:recon`, `reviewer`, `mutator`, `exit-gate` | Only inside `smith:implement` (recon, implementer, mutator, reviewer, exit-gate). | Skill never invoked; `implementer` called alone per task (35 times). |
40	| `sentinel:recon/verifier/exit-gate` | Only inside `sentinel:gate`. | Skill never invoked; no other path leads there. |
41	| `scribe:verifier` | Separate skill `scribe:verify-spec`, a distinct step between `draft-spec` and `audit-spec`. | Assistant called `scribe:drafter` then `scribe:exit-gate` directly (orin 26597, 26723). |
42	| `scribe:arch-auditor` | Separate skill `scribe:audit-architecture`. | Same skip. |
43	| Used: `muse:*` | All three agents in one skill, `muse:component`. | Skill loaded in pages. In orin the agents were called directly, and `muse:auditor` ran only once. |
44	| Used: `navigator:*`, `scribe:drafter/exit-gate`, `smith:implementer` | Self-contained "do one thing" agents whose descriptions read as direct delegation targets. | Called directly as personas. |
45	
46	The unused agents are those reachable only through a skill that was never invoked, or through a skipped step of the scribe chain. The used agents are those an orchestrator can pick from the agent list without a skill.
47	
48	## Verdict on the hypothesis: PARTLY CONFIRMED (mostly confirmed)
49	
50	Confirmed:
51	- Orin has 0 `Skill` calls in 36k lines. Pages has 1 plugin skill call in 63k lines. The pipelines were hand-composed from agents.
52	- The never-used agents are exactly those gated behind the uninvoked skills (`smith:implement`, `sentinel:gate`) or behind skipped steps of the scribe chain.
53	- The one plugin skill that was loaded (`muse:component`) ran its full pipeline.
54	
55	Qualified:
56	- "Skills unavailable" is refuted: they were listed in both sessions.
57	- Skipping skills is not the whole cause. `muse:*` also ran directly in orin. The shared cause is that the assistant treated plugins as a cast of agents (Muse, Navigator, Smith, Sentinel) and sequenced them itself, a habit the agent descriptions invite.
58	- Whether cost or stalls drove the omission of reviewer/mutator is not shown. The digests record 17 failed agent tasks and many "stalled" streams, and a repo-wide pre-commit gate that "cost me about a dozen waits" (pages 21361), but no assistant text links these to skipping. Treat as unknown.
59	- Later, the user directed less ceremony (pages 49946, 14 Oct: "lean less on the specs and tests"). That explains the dropped gates after 14 Oct, not the earlier skipped Smith steps.
60	
61	## Impact (only where evidence supports it)
62	
63	- No implementation review, independent exit-gate verdict or baseline recon ever ran on `smith:implementer` output. Verdicts came from the implementers themselves and the orchestrator.
64	- Defects were found after the fact by human-directed review or late e2e rather than by a plugin gate (D-outcomes.md items 1, 2, 7, 8):
65	  - Orin 3 Oct review (36196): "the tests assert markup, so all 29 twx tests pass with every defect below present". This is the weakness `smith:mutator` survivor analysis targets. Caveat: the code reviewed was Codex's, not `smith:implementer`'s, so it shows the pattern, not a Smith miss.
66	  - SiteNav logo-cap regression (AC-112, AC-017) was caught only by a manual `just e2e` run (orin 36113-36143); Playwright is `runInCI: false`.
67	  - Pages: spec/code drift at the 760px boundary, where 296 nav-fixture tests pinned the wrong constant (D-outcomes item 2); contrast and target-size defects found by the first automated suite four days after base specs passed (item 7); e2e work surfaced 6 product defects and two were "fixed as spec exemptions" by changing the spec (C-pages-sessions, pages ~21276).
68	- Not supported: that `smith:reviewer`, `mutator` or `exit-gate` would have caught these. The evidence shows a verification gap those agents are designed for (test discrimination, sibling and family search, current-state check), not a demonstrated catch.
69	- The spec side also skipped `verify-spec` and `audit-architecture`. Drift between SPEC-001/003a/003c and shipped code (D-outcomes item 1) is what `audit-architecture` and `spec-drift` target; again plausible, not shown. The drafting gates that did run produced many real blockers (118 across re-gates, pages 22772), so spec quality was not neglected overall.
70	
71	## Recommendations
72	
73	1. Make skills the entry point. State in the harness instructions and each plugin README: "For plugin work, call the plugin's Skill; call its agents directly only when the skill says so." The skills already hold order, retry limits and routing that the orchestrator re-derived by hand.
74	2. Rewrite agent descriptions that read "Delegate to this subagent when..." to mark skill-internal steps: "Step N of `smith:implement`; do not call alone". Prioritize `smith:implementer`, `navigator:*`, `scribe:drafter/exit-gate`, the agents actually called directly. Hide internal agents from the model-visible agent list if the harness allows.
75	3. Fold the scribe chain (draft, verify, audit, architecture, gate) into one pipeline skill with optional steps marked, like `muse:component` and `sentinel:gate`. Today `verifier` and `arch-auditor` sit behind separate skills that nothing triggers.
76	4. Add a router skill mapping intent to pipeline: component spec -> `muse:component`; plan -> `navigator:plan`; implement -> `smith:implement`; "use our plugins" / "quality work" -> the lifecycle in order, ending at `sentinel:gate`. The prompt at orin 20776 matched no skill trigger phrase.
77	5. In `smith:implement`, forbid calling `smith:implementer` alone. If cost or stalls are the real barrier, define an explicit light mode (recon and exit-gate only) instead of letting steps drop silently.
78	6. Make skipping visible: the pipeline's final artifact should list which gates ran and which were skipped, so "Sentinel gates" cannot be promised (pages 14940) and then silently dropped.
79	7. Add a `mason:evaluate` check for the pattern: a smith agent call with no `smith:implement` Skill call, or a spec exit-gate with no preceding verify/audit.
80	8. Log plugin skill and agent use per session (the `rows.json` scan is enough) so non-use is observable without manual investigation.
81
